summary: Completed the read-only Sites-to-Cloudflare deployment handover investigation and recorded verified facts in docs/DEPLOY_HANDOVER_FACTS.md without writing any secret value or changing Sites, Worker, D1, environment, access, domain, owner, group, or indexing state. Production logs identify Worker axie-b-ac--sgg-player-archive in Cloudflare account 7979fbd212715c4874b937da9cb25d4f, while the Cloudflare account currently authenticated through Wrangler is 8b32932649804bcee9bbcd58c7ddd1a0; a read-only deployment lookup confirms the production Worker does not exist in that owner-side account. Sites exposes only the logical D1 binding DB, so the production database_id, source database name, owner control, and Dashboard visibility remain unknown. The owner-side account contains a D1 named sgg-player-os with ID d49f95b5-3f70-4f43-9673-9a1eb0ae1e02, but its observed schema stops at players, point_grants, and audit_events and does not establish production identity. Sites environment revision 2 contains nine configured names, recorded only by name and secret classification. Cloudflare officially supports Wrangler Worker deployment, D1 bindings, and remote D1 SQL export, but the same Sites Worker/D1 cannot currently be managed directly because the production account is inaccessible through the present credential and the physical D1 identifier is unavailable.

Production Worker logs identify a Cloudflare account that is not present in the current owner-side Wrangler account list, and the production Worker is not readable from the owner-side account. The separate owner-side sgg-player-os D1 lacks current schema evidence and is not verified as production.
